## Best Practices for Conversation Relay Provider Failover


When you're scaling Voice AI agents in production[using Twilio Conversation Relay](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/conversationrelay) , keeping your architecture uninterrupted is critical. That’s *especially* true during high-volume events like Black Friday or Cyber Monday, or sudden traffic spikes. High load or unexpected provider degradation can introduce latencies, connection drops, or request failures. To harden your Conversation Relay infrastructure against these risks, you need an application-level failover strategy.


[Conversation Relay](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/twiml/connect/conversationrelay) uses two speech providers on every call: a **transcription (ASR/STT)** provider that turns the caller's speech into text, and a **text-to-speech (TTS)** provider that speaks your agent's replies. Each one is a third-party service, such as Deepgram, Google, ElevenLabs, or Amazon. Sometimes, a service might be slow, unavailable, or reject a request.


This guide covers:


- How a provider failure reaches your application, at startup and mid-call.
- Which error codes to look for.
- How to return new` <ConversationRelay>` TwiML from your` action` URL that **fails over** to a different provider, so the caller stays on the line.
- How to deal with failures in the middle of a call by sending an` end` message with` handoffData` , then switching providers in the TwiML that follows.


## How failures reach you


Where a failure shows up depends on **which provider** failed and **when** it failed:


When Provider What Conversation Relay does Where you see it


Startup Transcription (ASR) Ends the session. **` action` URL** :` SessionStatus=failed` and an` ErrorCode`


Startup (welcome greeting) Text-to-speech (TTS) Usually ends the session. If the failure arrives just after the call connects, it's reported like a mid-call TTS failure instead (next row). **` action` URL** :` SessionStatus=failed` and an` ErrorCode` , **or** a WebSocket` error` message


Mid-call Transcription (ASR) Ends the session. **` action` URL** : an` ErrorCode` (` SessionStatus` may be` failed` **or**` ended` )


Mid-call Text-to-speech (TTS) **Keeps the call up.** The failed reply is not spoken, and later replies are tried again. **WebSocket` error` message only.** Your server decides whether to end the session.


Two rules follow from this table:


- **In your` action` URL handler, check` ErrorCode` , not only` SessionStatus` .** Some mid-call failures report` SessionStatus=ended` and still include an` ErrorCode` .
- **Handle TTS failures in your WebSocket server.** When the agent's voice stops working mid-call, the call stays connected and the caller hears silence. Conversation Relay won't end the call for you. Your server has to notice the` error` messages and send` end` (see the **Mid-call failures section** , below).


## Prerequisites for failover


Before implementing custom failover logic, your Conversation Relay application should implement a few basic best practices. These fundamentals will help you build a robust production service.


### Always set an action URL on <Connect>


Failover only works when an` action` URL is set on` <Connect>` . When the Conversation Relay session ends, for any reason, Twilio sends a request to that URL, and the call carries on with the TwiML you return. Without an` action` URL, the call moves on to whatever verb follows` <Connect>` in the original document, and you can't vary that by error.


Copy code


```text
<Response>
<Connect action="https://example.com/relay-ended?attempt=1">
<ConversationRelay url="wss://example.com/agent" ... />
</Connect>
</Response>
```


### Name your providers explicitly


Always set` ttsProvider` and` transcriptionProvider` , even when you're using the defaults. That way every TwiML document says exactly which provider it uses, and your failover TwiML can switch to a different one.


If you leave out the TTS or transcription settings for a language, Conversation Relay fills them from a default (ElevenLabs with a default voice for TTS; Google or Deepgram for transcription). That default is not something you can fail over from or to on purpose. Set` ttsProvider` next to` voice` as well, rather than letting the provider be inferred from the voice name.


### Track the attempt number


Put the attempt number, and which providers you've already tried, in the` action` URL query string (for example` ?attempt=2&tts=google` ). Your handler then knows where it is in the failover chain and can't end up in a loop (see the **Avoiding failover loops** section for more).


## Watch your action URL parameters


When the session ends,[Twilio sends the standard Voice call parameters](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/api/call-resource#statuscallback) (` CallSid` ,` AccountSid` ,` From` ,` To` ,` CallStatus` , and so on) plus these Conversation Relay parameters:


Parameter Present Description


` SessionId` Always ID of the Conversation Relay session that ended.


` SessionStatus` Always` completed` : the caller hung up.` ended` : the session was ended, normally by your` end` message.` failed` : the session ended because of an error.


` SessionDuration` Always How long the session lasted, in seconds.


` ErrorCode` On error Twilio error code. **Branch on this.**


` ErrorMessage` On error Human-readable description. It can include the provider's own error text. Log it, but don't branch on it, because the wording can change.


` HandoffData` When you sent it The` handoffData` string from your` end` message, passed through unchanged.


### Error codes to watch


Some error codes you’ll get back from the webhook suggest it’s time for you to fail over to another provider. This section has an overview of the types of codes you may see, plus the individual error codes.


#### Provider failures: candidates for failover


Code Meaning Typical cause Recommended action


**64114** Unable to connect to ASR provider The transcription provider is unreachable, timed out during setup, or failed during the call. **Fail over transcription** to a different` transcriptionProvider` .


**64111** TTS provider service error The TTS provider returned a server error (5xx), timed out, or dropped the connection. This usually means a provider outage or slowdown. **Fail over TTS** to a different` ttsProvider` .


**64112** TTS provider conversion error The TTS provider rejected the request, for example because the voice ID doesn't exist, the credentials or quota are invalid, or the text or settings aren't supported.` ErrorMessage` (or the WebSocket` description` ) includes the provider's reason. **Fail over TTS** to keep the caller on the line, **and** check your voice and provider configuration. This error usually happens again with the same settings. **Exception:** if the message contains` input_timeout_exceeded` , see the **64112** section below.


**64103** Internal server error Something failed inside Twilio, not at your speech provider. Provider failures are reported with 64111, 64112, and 64114 instead. Retry **once** with the same providers. If the error keeps happening, contact Twilio Support with the` CallSid` .


**Upgrading an existing handler?** Earlier versions of Conversation Relay reported many provider failures as **64103** , and Google or Amazon voice rejections as **64106** . Handlers that retry 64103 once keep working, but branching on 64111, 64112, and 64114 is now enough to catch provider failures.


#### Other codes you may see in the same handler


Code Meaning Suggested handling


64102 Unable to connect to WebSocket URL Fail over to a backup WebSocket URL (` url=` ), not to a different speech provider.


64105 WebSocket session ended Your server closed the WebSocket without sending` end` . Send` end` instead (see the **Mid-call failures** section).


64107 Invalid message received Your server sent a malformed message. Fix the server.


64104 Max call duration reached Expected behavior. No failover.


## Startup failures


A *startup failure* means the session ended before the conversation got going. Usually the caller has heard nothing yet, or only part of the welcome greeting. Conversation Relay calls your` action` URL with` SessionStatus=failed` and an` ErrorCode` , and the caller **stays on the line** while you return new TwiML.


### Original TwiML (primary providers)


Copy code


```text
<Response>
<Connect action="https://example.com/relay-ended?attempt=1&stt=deepgram&tts=elevenlabs">
<ConversationRelay
url="wss://example.com/agent"
transcriptionProvider="Deepgram"
speechModel="nova-3-general"
ttsProvider="ElevenLabs"
voice="YOUR_ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID"
language="en-US"
welcomeGreeting="Hi! Thanks for calling. How can I help you today?" />
</Connect>
</Response>
```


*Escape*` &` *as*` &` *inside XML attribute values.*


### Transcription (ASR) failed at startup: ErrorCode=64114


Keep the TTS provider and switch the transcription provider:


Copy code


```text
<Response>
<Connect action="https://example.com/relay-ended?attempt=2&stt=google&tts=elevenlabs">
<ConversationRelay
url="wss://example.com/agent"
transcriptionProvider="Google"
speechModel="telephony"
ttsProvider="ElevenLabs"
voice="YOUR_ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID"
language="en-US"
welcomeGreeting="Hi! Thanks for calling. How can I help you today?">
<Parameter name="failoverReason" value="stt-64114" />
</ConversationRelay>
</Connect>
</Response>
```


When you switch transcription providers, also change` speechModel` to a model the new provider supports. A Deepgram model name sent to Google, or the other way round, fails with **64106** .


### TTS failed at startup: ErrorCode=64111 or 64112


Keep the transcription provider and switch the TTS provider and voice:


Copy code


```text
<Response>
<Connect action="https://example.com/relay-ended?attempt=2&stt=deepgram&tts=google">
<ConversationRelay
url="wss://example.com/agent"
transcriptionProvider="Deepgram"
speechModel="nova-3-general"
ttsProvider="Google"
voice="en-US-Journey-O"
language="en-US"
welcomeGreeting="Hi! Thanks for calling. How can I help you today?">
<Parameter name="failoverReason" value="tts-64111" />
</ConversationRelay>
</Connect>
</Response>
```


Voices belong to a provider. When you change` ttsProvider` , choose a voice from the new provider's catalog. Pick your backup voice in advance, so the agent sounds as close as possible to the primary.


The backup provider must also support your` language` . Providers don't all serve the same languages, and a backup that doesn't (for example Amazon with` zh-TW` or` he-IL` ) is rejected with **64101** , which means your failover TwiML fails too. Test every backup voice for each language you support.


The` <Parameter>` elements are passed to your WebSocket server in the` setup` message under` customParameters` . That way your agent knows it's running on a failover session, and can, for example, keep the response style shorter or log the event.


### Example action URL handler


Here's a minimal Node.js (Express) handler. It picks the next provider, limits the number of attempts, and falls back to a human agent when nothing else works:


Copy code


```text
const express = require('express');
const app = express();
app.use(express.urlencoded({ extended: false }));


const STT = {
deepgram: { provider: 'Deepgram', speechModel: 'nova-3-general' },
google:   { provider: 'Google',   speechModel: 'telephony' },
};
const TTS = {
elevenlabs: { provider: 'ElevenLabs', voice: 'YOUR_ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID' },
google:     { provider: 'Google',     voice: 'en-US-Journey-O' },
amazon:     { provider: 'Amazon',     voice: 'Joanna-Neural' },
};
const NEXT_STT = { deepgram: 'google', google: 'deepgram' };
const NEXT_TTS = { elevenlabs: 'google', google: 'amazon', amazon: 'elevenlabs' };
const MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3;


const ASR_CODES = new Set(['64114']);
const TTS_CODES = new Set(['64111', '64112']);
const RETRY_CODES = new Set(['64103']);
const FAILOVER_REASONS = new Set(['stt-failure', 'tts-failure', 'internal-error']);


app.post('/relay-ended', (req, res) => {
const { SessionStatus, ErrorCode, ErrorMessage, HandoffData, CallSid } = req.body;
const attempt = Number(req.query.attempt || 1);
let stt = req.query.stt || 'deepgram';
let tts = req.query.tts || 'elevenlabs';
res.type('text/xml');


// The caller hung up: nothing to do.
if (SessionStatus === 'completed') return res.send('<Response/>');


// A mid-call handoff from your WebSocket server (Mid-call failures section). Parse HandoffData first.
let handoff = {};
try { handoff = HandoffData ? JSON.parse(HandoffData) : {}; } catch (_) { /* not JSON */ }


// Provider failures from ErrorCode, or from your own handoff reasonCode (Mid-call failures section).
const reason = handoff.reasonCode
|| (ASR_CODES.has(ErrorCode) ? 'stt-failure'
: TTS_CODES.has(ErrorCode) ? 'tts-failure'
: RETRY_CODES.has(ErrorCode) ? 'internal-error'
: null);


if (ErrorCode) console.warn(`CallSid=${CallSid} ErrorCode=${ErrorCode} ErrorMessage=${ErrorMessage}`);


// Only the explicit failover reasons start a new ConversationRelay. Everything else
// (normal end, configuration errors like 64101/64106, live-agent, llm-failure, ...) is
// not a provider failure, so it goes to handleNormalEnd.
if (!FAILOVER_REASONS.has(reason)) return res.send(handleNormalEnd({ reason, ErrorCode, handoff }));
if (attempt >= MAX_ATTEMPTS) return res.send(finalFallback());


if (reason === 'stt-failure') stt = NEXT_STT[stt];
if (reason === 'tts-failure') tts = NEXT_TTS[tts];
// 'internal-error': retry the same providers once.


res.send(relayTwiml({ attempt: attempt + 1, stt, tts, reason, handoff }));
});


function relayTwiml({ attempt, stt, tts, reason, handoff }) {
const s = STT[stt], t = TTS[tts];
const action = `https://example.com/relay-ended?attempt=${attempt}&stt=${stt}&tts=${tts}`;
// A mid-call failover resumes the conversation, so don't greet the caller again.
const greeting = handoff.conversationId
? 'Sorry about that, I had a brief technical issue. Where were we?'
: 'Hi! Thanks for calling. How can I help you today?';
return `<Response>
<Connect action="${action}">
<ConversationRelay url="wss://example.com/agent"
transcriptionProvider="${s.provider}" speechModel="${s.speechModel}"
ttsProvider="${t.provider}" voice="${t.voice}"
language="en-US" welcomeGreeting="${greeting}">
<Parameter name="failoverReason" value="${reason}" />
<Parameter name="conversationId" value="${handoff.conversationId || ''}" />
</ConversationRelay>
</Connect>
</Response>`;
}


function finalFallback() {
return `<Response>
<Say>We're sorry, we're having trouble right now. Connecting you to an agent.</Say>
<Dial>+15555550100</Dial>
</Response>`;
}


function handleNormalEnd({ reason, ErrorCode, handoff }) {
// Not a provider failure: the default path. Branch on your own handoff reasons (Ending the call for other mid-call reasons section).
if (reason === 'live-agent') return '<Response><Dial>+15555550100</Dial></Response>';
if (reason === 'llm-failure') return '<Response><Say>Sorry, something went wrong. Goodbye.</Say><Hangup/></Response>';
// A configuration error (64101, 64106, ...) won't be fixed by retrying: alert and end the call safely.
if (ErrorCode) return finalFallback();
return '<Response><Hangup/></Response>';
}
```


In production, escape every value you put into XML, and use the Twilio helper library or a TwiML builder rather than string templates where you can. Validate the` X-Twilio-Signature` header on every request to your` action` URL.


## Mid-call failures


Sometimes, you’ll need to react to a failure in the middle of a call. The following sections detail failure modes you could run into during a live call and detail whether you should take action.


### Mid-call transcription failure: no additional action needed in your WebSocket server


If the transcription provider fails during the call, Conversation Relay ends the session and calls your` action` URL with` ErrorCode=64114` (or` 64103` if the failure was inside Twilio). Depending on where in the call the failure happened,` SessionStatus` may be` failed` or` ended` . Your WebSocket connection is closed.


The` action` URL handler from the **Example action URL handler** section above already deals with this: it sees the ASR error code and returns TwiML with the other` transcriptionProvider` . To carry on the conversation instead of starting over, store your conversation state server-side (keyed by` CallSid` ) and look it up again when the new session's` setup` message arrives.` setup` always includes` callSid` .


### Mid-call TTS failure: your WebSocket server must act


A mid-call TTS failure **does not end the session** . Conversation Relay sends an` error` message to your WebSocket server, doesn't speak that reply, and keeps the call connected. If the provider is down, every later reply fails the same way, and the caller hears silence until they hang up.


The` error` message comes in one of two forms, depending on the provider:


Copy code


```text
{
"type": "error",
"description": "Error converting tokens to speech, code: 64111, error: <provider error>, tokens: Sure, your appointment is on Tuesday at 3 PM."
}
```


Copy code


```text
{
"type": "error",
"description": "Error playing media, code: 64112, error: TTS provider rejected the request due to invalid parameters: <provider error>"
}
```


The first form is used by most providers, including ElevenLabs and Deepgram. The second is used by Google and Amazon voices, and it doesn't include the unspoken text. Both include the **error code** (` code: ...` ). When the first form also includes the **text that couldn't be spoken** (` tokens: ...` ), you can pass it to the new session so the caller hears the reply they missed.


**Recommended handling:**


- Read the code from` description` . Treat` 64111` and` 64112` as TTS failures, whichever form the message takes. Skip` 64112` with` input_timeout_exceeded` (see the **Error codes to watch** section). Other codes, such as` 64106` for a media URL that couldn't be played, aren't provider failures.
- Decide when to fail over. A single 64111 can be a one-off. Two failures in a row, or any failure during the first turn (the welcome greeting), means the provider can't be relied on, so fail over.
- Send an **` end` message** with` handoffData` that describes why you're ending and what the next session needs.` handoffData` must be a **string** , so call` JSON.stringify` on your object.
- Conversation Relay ends the session and calls your` action` URL with` SessionStatus=ended` and` HandoffData` set to your string. Your handler returns TwiML that uses a different` ttsProvider` .


The` end` message:


Copy code


```text
{
"type": "end",
"handoffData": "{\"reasonCode\":\"tts-failure\",\"errorCode\":\"64111\",\"failedTtsProvider\":\"elevenlabs\",\"conversationId\":\"conv_8f2c\",\"unspokenText\":\"Sure, your appointment is on Tuesday at 3 PM.\"}"
}
```


### Example WebSocket server logic (Node.js, ws )


Copy code


```text
const { WebSocketServer } = require('ws');
const wss = new WebSocketServer({ port: 8080 });


const TTS_ERROR_CODES = new Set([64111, 64112]);
const MAX_CONSECUTIVE_TTS_ERRORS = 2;


wss.on('connection', (ws) => {
const session = { conversationId: null, consecutiveTtsErrors: 0, turns: 0, ending: false };


ws.on('message', (raw) => {
const msg = JSON.parse(raw);


switch (msg.type) {
case 'setup':
// Resume an existing conversation after a failover, or start a new one.
session.conversationId = msg.customParameters?.conversationId || newConversationId(msg.callSid);
break;


case 'prompt':
session.turns++;
session.consecutiveTtsErrors = 0; // the caller is being heard, so the conversation is still going
handlePrompt(ws, session, msg);   // your LLM logic; replies are sent as {type:'text', token, last}
break;


case 'error':
handleError(ws, session, msg.description || '');
break;
}
});
});


function handleError(ws, session, description) {
const match = description.match(/code:\s*(\d+)/);
const code = match ? Number(match[1]) : null;
// Matches both "Error converting tokens to speech" and "Error playing media" (Google/Amazon).
const isTtsError = TTS_ERROR_CODES.has(code) && !description.includes('input_timeout_exceeded');
if (!isTtsError || session.ending) return;


session.consecutiveTtsErrors++;
const failedOnGreeting = session.turns === 0;
if (!failedOnGreeting && session.consecutiveTtsErrors < MAX_CONSECUTIVE_TTS_ERRORS) return;


const unspoken = description.split(', tokens: ')[1] || ''; // empty for Google/Amazon messages
session.ending = true;
ws.send(JSON.stringify({
type: 'end',
handoffData: JSON.stringify({
reasonCode: 'tts-failure',
errorCode: String(code),
conversationId: session.conversationId,
unspokenText: unspoken.slice(0, 500),
}),
}));
}
```


### Handling the handoff in your action URL


The handler above already reads` HandoffData` . When` reasonCode` is` tts-failure` , it moves on to the next TTS provider. It also passes` conversationId` through a` <Parameter>` , so the new session's` setup` message resumes the same conversation. Here's the TwiML for a mid-call TTS handoff that also replays the unspoken text:


Copy code


```text
<Response>
<ConversationRelay
url="wss://example.com/agent"
transcriptionProvider="Deepgram"
speechModel="nova-3-general"
ttsProvider="Google"
voice="en-US-Journey-O"
language="en-US"
welcomeGreeting="Sorry about that, I had a brief technical issue. Sure, your appointment is on Tuesday at 3 PM.">
<Parameter name="failoverReason" value="tts-failure" />
<Parameter name="conversationId" value="conv_8f2c" />
</ConversationRelay>
</Connect>
</Response>
```


Putting` unspokenText` in` welcomeGreeting` means the caller hears the reply that failed. If you'd rather not, use a short "where were we?" greeting, or leave` welcomeGreeting` out and have your agent speak first once` setup` arrives.


### Ending the call for other mid-call reasons


You can use the same` end` plus` handoffData` pattern for any mid-call problem your server detects, for example when your LLM provider is down, a tool call keeps failing, or the caller asks for a person. Set a different` reasonCode` (` llm-failure` ,` live-agent` , ...) and branch on it in your` action` URL handler. Always prefer` end` to closing the WebSocket. If you close the WebSocket, the session fails with **64105** and you lose the` HandoffData` .


## Avoiding failover loops


When you add failovers to your Conversation Relay app, you need to be careful that you don’t accidentally create a loop which cycles through fallback providers and never exits. This list contains our best practices for avoiding a failover loop.


- **Limit the number of attempts.** Carry` attempt` in the` action` URL and stop after 2 or 3.
- **Change something on every attempt.** Only retry identical TwiML for 64103, and only once.
- **Don't fail over on configuration errors** (64101, 64106). They fail the same way on every attempt.
- **Always have a final fallback that doesn't use Conversation Relay** , such as` <Say>` with a` <Dial>` to a human agent,` <Enqueue>` ,` <Record>` for voicemail, or a polite` <Hangup>` .` <Say>` uses Twilio's own TTS, so it doesn't depend on the provider that just failed.
- **Return` <Response/>` when` SessionStatus=completed`** , because the caller has already hung up.


## Checklist


Looking for a cheatsheet on how to handle failovers in your production Conversation Relay app? This list contains a succinct version of our advice from this post, so you can check that your app is handling possible failure cases.


- ☐ Every` <Connect>` has an` action` URL that carries` attempt` and the current providers.
- ☐` ttsProvider` ,` voice` ,` transcriptionProvider` , and` speechModel` are set explicitly.
- ☐ A backup voice and a backup speech model are chosen and tested for each language you support. A backup that doesn't serve the language fails with 64101.
- ☐ The` action` URL handler branches on` ErrorCode` (not only` SessionStatus` ) and parses` HandoffData` .
- ☐ 64114 fails over transcription. 64111 and 64112 fail over TTS. 64103 retries once. 64101 and 64106 go to the fallback and get alerted on.
- ☐ Your WebSocket server watches for` error` messages with 64111 or 64112 (in both message forms) and sends` end` with` handoffData` .
- ☐ Conversation state is stored server-side and resumed through` <Parameter name="conversationId">` .
- ☐ The final fallback doesn't depend on Conversation Relay.
- ☐` ErrorCode` ,` ErrorMessage` , and` CallSid` are logged for every failover, so you can follow up with Twilio Support.


## Conclusion


By implementing these failover strategies, your Conversation Relay Voice AI agents will be more resilient against speech provider outages, traffic surges, and transient degradations. Building a multi-provider fallback strategy helps ensure continuous, high-availability conversation flow – whether you’re dealing with high-volume events like Black Friday, or traffic on a random weeknight.


With these best practices in place, your voice infrastructure can be hardened for enterprise scale. *We can’t wait to see – and hear – what you build!*
